messages.subject: What do these warnings mean?
parts:
Hi ,

I started on the Rstan 2.8 version (Which semms even awesomer BTW).....and ran a model that i have run several times before with version 2.6 and version 2.7. The only difference apart from the version is that I used 4 cores parallely. I'm getting these warnings I've never seen before. The results/ parameter distributions look ok and as expected, so I do not know If I am even suppossed to act on these?:

Warning messages:
1: There were 2000 transitions after warmup that exceeded the maximum treedepth. Increase max_treedepth.
2: Examine the pairs() plot to diagnose sampling problems

Any help will be appreciated! Thanks :)

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: What do these warnings mean?
parts:
On Thursday, October 8, 2015 at 5:45:27 AM UTC-4, UD1989 wrote:
I'm getting these warnings I've never seen before.
These warnings weren't thrown prior to 2.8.0 but the behavior was probably the same (i.e. not good).
The results/ parameter distributions look ok and as expected, so I do not know If I am even suppossed to act on these?:

Warning messages:
1: There were 2000 transitions after warmup that exceeded the maximum treedepth. Increase max_treedepth.
2: Examine the pairs() plot to diagnose sampling problems

You should specify control = list(max_treedepth = 15) in the call to stan() or some other number greater than 10 to allow the sampler to make more leapfrog steps per iteration. When it hits the maximum treedepth, you essentially cannot get from one part of the parameter space to another part of the parameter space in one iteration, which increases the dependence among the draws and may bias the draws relative to the true posterior distribution. The problematic points are shown in yellow if you call pairs() on the stanfit object but in this case, it looks as if all the transitions are problematic.

Ben
